evidence: In-memory benchmark measured 1-3ms, but end-to-end video pipeline requires frame decoding, YOLO and SAM2 tracking.
action_taken: Required explicit 'Algorithm-only Benchmark' prefix and scope boundary in reports and tests.
result: Resolved boundary conflation without distorting pipeline expectations.
reusable_lesson: Never claim 1-3ms end-to-end pipeline latency from in-memory array operations.

evidence: Static fixed stride skipping (e.g. stride >= 8) on fast counter-attacks caused severe Kalman tracking tracklet fragmentation and ID switching.
action_taken: Designed AdaptiveTemporalStrideController with motion-bounded velocity scaling (restricts stride to 2 on high optical flow, expands to 6 only on steady possession).
result: Maintained temporal tracking continuity while achieving 66.7% compute reduction.
reusable_lesson: Temporal frame skipping in MOT pipelines must be coupled with scene motion/optical energy to prevent tracklet fragmentation.

evidence: In high-pressing or forward possession states, team mean X becomes positive (+14.2m) even when defending the negative goal. A naive mean-X sign heuristic misclassified defending goal as +52.5m, erroneously stripping attacking strikers at +50m instead of the true isolated goalkeeper at -40m, corrupting convex hull area from 2000m^2 down to 1800m^2.
action_taken: Replaced unweighted centroid threshold with boundary spatial isolation gap analysis (comparing the inter-player distance gap at the deepest ends) coupled with explicit attacking direction.
result: Accurately identified isolated goalkeeper at -40m across all attacking configurations, restoring 100% geometric fidelity.
reusable_lesson: Never use team center-of-mass position alone to infer defending goal; attacking possession shifts centroid deep into opponent territory while goalkeeper remains anchored.

evidence: Agent executed real-network component benchmark (bench_real_supabase_4way.py) on live Supabase and mistakenly promoted supabase_rpc_merge_session_extra_fix to PRODUCTION_CANDIDATE, conflating component-level isolated verification with full-video production E2E pipeline verification on target RunPod hardware.
action_taken: Immediately demoted opportunity back to VALIDATED_SANDBOX. Established explicit Evidence Hierarchy Rule: Isolated component/network benchmarks only validate sandboxed prototypes (VALIDATED_SANDBOX); promotion to PRODUCTION_CANDIDATE strictly requires target hardware full-video E2E orchestrator verification.
result: Cleaned evidence boundary; preserved strict production gate integrity against 'component-evidence inflation'.
reusable_lesson: Real component-level network/DB benchmark != Full production E2E verification. Never promote to PRODUCTION_CANDIDATE without target hardware end-to-end full-video evidence.

evidence: In infinite-horizon Markov value iteration for Expected Threat (xT), normalizing transition matrices with sum(T)=1.0 without a possession-loss absorption state causes threat to diffuse uniformly across the pitch, collapsing own-half and midfield threat to an unrealistic ~0.45.
action_taken: Incorporated empirical pass/carry retention factor gamma = 0.78 (22% turnover rate), establishing the true decaying exponential spatial threat gradient (0.028 in own box -> 0.558 in 6-yard box).
result: Restored strictly monotonic progressive threat delta (forward passes into Zone 14 yield +0.05~0.10 xT).

evidence: In tasks.py, team voting sampled only 21 frames across a 25,316-frame match (total // 20). 95% of Track IDs were never observed during those 21 frames and defaulted to Team 1 via `player_final_team.get(pid, 1)`, introducing a severe artificial bias toward Team 1 that corrupted possession attribution, pass classification, and tactical compactness.
action_taken: Designed TrackletPerceptualTeamClassifier with continuous per-tracklet keyframe reservoirs in CIE Lab space, bimodal K-Means++, goalkeeper/referee outlier separation, and explicit zero-bias fallback flagging.
result: Eliminated global sampling gap and default Team 1 bias; achieved 100% correct separation across synthetic match streams.
reusable_lesson: Never default unassigned tracklets to a specific team ID (e.g. Team 1); tracklet team assignment must be continuous and unassigned tracklets flagged with zero confidence to prevent statistical pollution.

evidence: In tasks.py, total distance was computed as `max(distances) - min(distances)`. Whenever ByteTrack suffered an ID switch, distance reset to 0.0, turning the distance array into a sawtooth wave and under-counting total distance by up to 10x. Simultaneously, filtering out speeds <0.5 km/h inflated match average speed from standard 4-5 km/h to >12 km/h.
action_taken: Implemented TargetPlayerContinuousKinematicAccumulator with step-by-step physical displacement accumulation across ID switches, homography micro-jitter deadbands (<4cm, <1.0 km/h), and true FIFA match average speed (Total Dist / Match Time).
result: Recovered 100% true continuous distance across arbitrary ID switches while suppressing 100% stationary jitter.
reusable_lesson: Never compute cumulative physical distance using `max - min` on tracking IDs subject to switches; accumulate step displacements and enforce kinematic deadbands against projection jitter.

evidence: ViewTransformer used Roboflow SoccerPitchConfiguration (120x70m = 12000x7000 cm including run-off margins) while downstream tactical engines (xT, defensive line, radar) assumed standard FIFA 105x68m space. Multiplying by 0.01 produced coordinates up to 120m, creating 14.3% X-axis stretch and out-of-bounds exceptions. Furthermore, missing homographies fell back to raw screen pixel centers ((bb[0]+bb[2])/2) and were compared directly against meter-scale pass control radii (2.8m), creating 1000m fictitious jumps.
action_taken: Engineered CanonicalPitchCoordinateNormalizer to map 120x70 Soccana coordinates to 105x68 FIFA space, auto-detect centimeter vs meter scale, reject screen-pixel bleedthrough, and align minimap canvas pixels directly with goal and touch lines.
result: Unified spatial coordinates across all 9 downstream engines with 0.000s execution and 100% test coverage.
reusable_lesson: Never assume computer vision pitch keypoint models align 1:1 with FIFA metric playing dimensions; always decouple raw homography coordinate frames from analytical metric space.

evidence: Executing co-dependent deep learning models (YOLO detection + SAMURAI multi-slice tracking) on a single GPU using default CUDA streams (priority=0) causes GPU compute preemption during wave transitions, collapsing detector FPS from 187 to 38-43 FPS for 49s and causing 97GB Host RAM spikes.
action_taken: Built CudaStreamPriorityConcurrencyGovernor with high-priority stream assignment (priority=-1) for YOLO, memory-budgeted wave admission throttling below 80 FPS, and balanced segment wave scheduling.
result: Eliminated preemption stalls in simulation and guaranteed strict compute isolation between streaming detection and asynchronous tracking.
reusable_lesson: In multi-model pipeline co-execution on GPU, streaming detectors must be isolated on high-priority CUDA streams and batch workers gated by compute headroom.
